prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper), North Bay Controller, South Bay Controller automate bays; Juniper enforces permissives/interlocks, timestamps state changes, produces Bay Status Digest. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized/interlocked operations; control failure cannot inhibit protection. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects feeders, produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) displays indications/communications quality separately from archived evidence; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip. Station Gateway carries authorized supervisory communications. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) aligns time, produces Clock Drift Snapshot. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard) preserves authoritative evidence. Engineering Workstation provides approved search/filter/export tools, restricts engineers, revision-controls configurations/history, produces Settings Review Receipt. Maintenance Remote Terminal grants approved access without local authority. Station DC System powers automation/protection, produces Battery Load Test Record for engineering-record retention.
Actors: Control Room Operator verifies commands/field conditions, coordinates access, suspends work, reviews event sequences, submits switching requests specifying equipment/state-changes/timing. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) maintains station-wide switching plan, coordinates both bays, checks clearance/work conflicts, confirms handback. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) develops changes, compares event times/relay indications, uses Relay Diagnostic Note. Substation Supervisor authorizes changes/escalates availability. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) performs authorized work, sends Breaker Inspection Tag(condition/time).
Requirements: Local selection/interlocks prevail; remote commands require authority/permissions/availability. Communications loss means stale/unavailable displays; verify recovery. Timing never governs protection; retain reference-loss evidence, quality, original ordering/source/timestamps; flag uncertainty, discontinuity, corrected/estimated times. Queries should bound station/equipment/time; exports preserve timestamps/quality; label derived ordering, separate conclusions. Archive access authorized; administration/configuration/access auditable; retention scheduled; investigation holds authority-released; check capacity/ingestion/recoverability, test readable restoration preserving timestamp/quality; protected backup; post-handback evidence reviewable.
Settings require documented basis/coordination, unique revision, independent qualified review, approval, model/firmware verification, approved window, installed comparison/testing, discrepancy resolution. Work requires authorization, hazard/route/communications review, attendance logs, boundaries, physical identity/isolation/energy verification; uncertainty reported/resolved; communications loss stops affected work.

New part:
S127: The Substation Supervisor resolves priority conflicts and confirms the operational authority for exceptional switching conditions.
S128: Approved switching sequences identify the required order of actions, hold points, and conditions for stopping work.
S129: The North Bay Controller manages control and interlocking functions assigned to the north bay under the approved sequence.
S130: The North Bay Controller blocks a close command when its local interlocks indicate that the bay is not ready.
S131: The South Bay Controller manages the corresponding control and interlocking functions assigned to the south bay.
S132: The two controllers have separate equipment scopes and do not substitute for one another when executing a switching sequence.
S133: The bay boundary defines which controller may operate each device and which indications are used to confirm its state.
S134: Equipment shared across the boundary requires explicit coordination before a switching action can affect either bay.
S135: The Bay Automation Controller presents bay control status while preserving the separate operating scopes of the two controllers.
S136: The Breaker Control Unit executes permitted breaker commands only when the applicable control conditions are satisfied.
S137: The North Protection Panel supports protection functions for the north-side equipment within its assigned scope.
S138: The Transformer Protection Panel retains its protection authority independently of the bay switching sequence.
S139: The Station Supervisory Control System uses the status digest to review current station operating conditions.
S140: The Sequence Event Archive receives the Clock Drift Snapshot for event-time correlation.
S141: The Switching Desk Coordinator produces the Isolation Boundary Card for the planned work.
S142: The Station Gateway produces the Protocol Retry Summary for communication review.
S143: Larkspur reviews protection coordination questions that could affect the planned switching sequence.
S144: Bluefin provides the station time reference used to align recorded event times.
S145: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S146: After the Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback, state-change evidence remains available for authorized engineering review.
S147: Alarm indications are assessed according to protection significance, equipment condition, and the potential effect on service.
S148: The Control Room Operator reviews the alarm priority, source, time, and associated bay indications before deciding on a response.
S149: The operator distinguishes a new alarm from a standing condition and checks whether related indications support the same assessment.
S150: For a protection operation or an unexplained equipment state, the Control Room Operator treats the condition as requiring prompt investigation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
